text: Hi, how's it going? I'm a big coffee lover, so I guess I'll start there. I can't really start my day without a cup of coffee, and this morning was no different. I had one before I came to take this test, and I'm already looking forward to another one once it's over. I work in IT, and my days are pretty busy. I live in an apartment, and I'm pretty much a homebody. In my free time, I like listening to music, playing computer games, and reading. So, yeah, that's me in a nutshell: coffee, music, and my computer. I'm happy to be here, and I hope I do well today!

One industry that's really on the rise is electric cars, especially the batteries inside them. I see more electric cars on the road every year, so I see it with my own eyes. Korea has been making batteries for decades, and we're known for high-quality, high-tech products. Lately, there's been a big push for cleaner energy, so countries around the world want cars that produce less pollution. Korean companies are among the best at making the batteries. On top of that, the industry is going digital. We're using AI and smart systems to make batteries faster and safer. That's why orders have been pouring in. It's a great time to be in this industry, and I'm excited to watch it grow.

The company I'd like to talk about is a big Korean battery maker. It's one of the top names in the world. Honestly, I might be a little biased, but I really think it's promising. First, it has strong technology, especially in long-lasting batteries and fast charging. Second, it keeps investing in the future, like new battery types and recycling. As for the benefits to society, there are a lot. It creates thousands of jobs, not just for the employees, but also for local restaurants, shops, and small suppliers. Whole towns depend on it. It also brings in a lot of money from exports, which helps the national economy. When the company does well, the country does well. That's why I'm proud of it, even as an outsider.

There have been a lot of changes recently. The biggest one is the digital transformation. They've introduced AI and smart systems to their factories, so they can track the production in real time. For example, they started using sensors and cameras to spot safety problems early. That has made the workplace safer. They've also started making more batteries for electric cars, which are in high demand right now. As a result, the company has received more orders, and the work has been getting busier. I read that it's been a lot of pressure for their teams. But it's exciting, because they're doing something new. I think these changes will make the company stronger in the long run.

I like K-pop concerts, especially girl group concerts, like my favorite group's. I'll be honest: I haven't been to many, but I love the idea of them. I like them for a few reasons. First, the energy is unreal. The lights, the dancing, and the crowd singing along: you just can't get that from a recording. Second, it's a great way to forget about work. For two hours, you're not thinking about servers or emails. And third, it makes me feel young again! I also like small outdoor concerts, where you can just relax on the grass. It's less crowded, and the atmosphere is friendly. If I could, I'd go to one every month.

To be honest, I started going to concerts pretty late. When I was young, I was always too busy studying, and later, too busy working. My real interest started when I became a fan of my favorite K-pop group. I'd watch their live performances on YouTube, and I'd think, "I wish I were there." Then one of my coworkers, who goes to concerts all the time, told me, "You have to feel it in person." That's what pushed me to try. My first real concert was just this year. Since then, I've been hooked. I wish I had started earlier! Now I check the concert schedule all the time, and I even set alerts for ticket sales. It's become a new hobby.

The last concert I went to was a free outdoor concert at a local festival in my city, just a few weeks ago. I went with a friend. The best part was that one of the guest performers was a member of my favorite group, and she's from my city! I was so excited, I could barely sit still. The stage was set up near the sea, and the sunset was behind it. It was a perfect fall evening. When she walked on stage, the whole crowd went wild. She said a few words about her hometown, and people cheered like crazy. I even sang along to a couple of songs. My friend teased me because she'd never seen me so excited. It wasn't a huge concert, but it was a night I'll always remember.

My favorite place in Korea is Tongyeong. It's close to my city, so it's easy to get to, but it feels like a different world. It's a port city with beautiful islands, and it's sometimes called "the Naples of Korea." I love it for three reasons. First, the scenery is stunning: you can ride a cable car up the mountain and look down at dozens of little islands. Second, the food is amazing, especially the fresh seafood. I always get the raw fish and a bowl of seafood stew. And third, there are lots of cute cafes with ocean views, which is perfect for a coffee lover like me. Whenever I need a mini getaway, I go to Tongyeong. It always makes me feel refreshed.

When I was in college, I went on a trip to Gangneung with three of my best friends. We were broke students, so we took the cheapest train we could find. We went there to see the sunrise at the beach, because we'd heard it was a famous spot. We stayed in a tiny, cheap room, and all four of us slept on the floor. We woke up at 5 a.m., freezing, and walked to the beach in the dark. When the sun finally came up over the ocean, nobody said a word. It was so beautiful. Then we ate hot noodles at a small stand, and it was the best thing I'd ever tasted. We didn't have much money, but we had so much fun. Those were the days!

Yes, one trip to Jeju Island stands out. My friend and I decided to hike Hallasan, the tallest mountain in Korea. The weather was perfect when we started. But about halfway up, the sky suddenly turned dark, and it started to hail! The hailstones were as big as peanuts, and they hurt! We had no umbrellas. We hid under a tree, but we were still getting hit. My friend started laughing and said, "This is what we get for not checking the forecast!" After about ten minutes, it stopped, and the sun came out. And just then, a huge rainbow appeared over the mountain. It was breathtaking. We were soaking wet and our legs were sore, but we were so happy. We finally reached a beautiful viewpoint, and we shared a hot cup of instant coffee from my backpack. It was the best coffee ever. That's why I never skip the weather forecast now!

Hello, I'd like to make an appointment for a health checkup. I have a few questions. First, what are your office hours? I work during the day, so I'm hoping to come in the evening or on a Saturday.. Okay. And is the doctor available next week?. Great. How long will the checkup take?. Also, do I need to fast before the visit? And should I bring anything, like my ID or insurance card?. Perfect. One last thing: how much does it cost?. That's very helpful. Thank you so much! I'll see you then.

Hello, I have an appointment tomorrow at 10 a.m., but I'm afraid I have to reschedule. Something came up at work. I have to give an important presentation to our executives, and it was moved to tomorrow morning. I'm really sorry about the short notice. Is there any chance I could come in later in the week? Thursday afternoon or Friday morning would work best for me. If those are full, how about next Monday? Or, if you have any cancellations, could you call me? I'd be happy to come in on short notice. Again, I apologize for the trouble. Thank you so much for your understanding!

I remember a time when I had to cancel an important appointment. It was a dental checkup, which I'd waited three weeks to get. But that morning, a typhoon was coming to the south coast. The winds were so strong that the bridge to the mainland was closed. And since the clinic was on the mainland, there was no way to get there. I was so annoyed. I called the clinic, explained the situation, and apologized. They were very understanding, and they said they get a lot of calls like that during typhoon season. We rescheduled for the following week. In the end, I spent the day at home, with a cup of coffee watching the rain. A friend told me, "Maybe it's the universe telling you to relax." She was right. Since then, I always check the weather before I book anything.

A country that's similar to Korea is Japan. Both countries are surrounded by water, and both have lots of mountains. There's not much flat land in either country, so people live close together in the cities. Japan also has thousands of islands, just like Korea. There are differences, of course: Japan is bigger, and it has more volcanoes and earthquakes. In recent years, Japan has changed a lot. The biggest change is probably tourism. The yen has become weaker, so Japan has become a very cheap place to visit. A lot of foreign tourists have been going there, including many Koreans. Also, the population is getting older, which is a big issue. Korea is facing the same problem. I visited Osaka years ago, and I'd love to go back to see how it's changed.

The most recent article I read about Japan was about the economy. I saw it on a news app on my phone during my coffee break. The article was about the weak yen and how it's affecting tourism. It said that record numbers of foreign tourists were visiting Japan, because everything has become so cheap for them. Hotels and restaurants were packed, and some popular spots were overcrowded. It also said that this was good for the economy, because tourism brings in a lot of money. But on the other hand, local people were getting frustrated, because prices were going up and the streets were too crowded. I found it interesting because Korea has a similar problem in popular tourist spots like Jeju. I think every country has to find a balance between tourism and quality of life.
